findings.claim: The rewrite resolves r1 W2-001 and r2 W1-003/W2-002 for a WebSocket-only path. Every method except OPTIONS now gets 426, HEAD agrees with GET, and the Allow set counts a WebSocket route as GET. Mixed paths are still open. Take a path with a WebSocket route and a POST route. A GET without Upgrade gets 405, because the path is not WebSocket-only, and the Allow header lists GET and HEAD, so the methods the 405 just refused appear in Allow. The section also never says how a request whose Upgrade value is not websocket (for example Upgrade: h2c) counts for the 'without Upgrade' check.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one rule for a path that has a WebSocket route and no HTTP GET route. Either it answers 426 to a plain GET/HEAD whatever other routes the path has, or the Allow set leaves GET/HEAD out when they come only from a WebSocket route. Also say that 'without Upgrade' means the request does not carry Upgrade: websocket. Add a router test for the mixed path.

findings.claim: The rewrite leaves part of r2 W2-005 open. The three path-form switches have defined matching effects, but the section does not say how they change the freeze-time conflict checks. With case-insensitive matching on, are GET /Users and GET /users a duplicate (D-056)? With trailing-slash ignoring on, do /a and /a/ conflict? The section says a TRACE/CONNECT route registered while the policy is disabled gets 'unsupported method'. It does not say whether that route's method still appears in the Allow union of D-061/D-064.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the freeze compares patterns after the active normalisation. Under it, /Users and /users are duplicates when case-insensitive matching is on, and /a and /a/ are duplicates when trailing slashes are ignored. Also say that a disabled TRACE/CONNECT route counts toward neither the Allow sets nor matching.

findings.claim: Two decisions cite the wrong frozen items. 'Path-form policy (D-054, D-070)' applies D-050 (the strict default) and D-053 (the router option). D-054 is literal-over-variable priority. 'Pattern validation (D-057, D-058)' extends the pattern grammar of D-047/D-048 (empty or repeated variable names), not the freeze-time duplicate checks.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel the two decisions as 'Path-form policy (D-050, D-053, D-070)' and 'Pattern validation (D-047, D-048)'.
